name: Norway
status: Twice negotiated entry, twice refused it by referendum — 1972 and 1994. In the single market through the EEA since 1994.
notes: Adopts most internal-market law without a vote on it. Agriculture and fisheries stay outside. Sovereign wealth fund founded 1990, first deposit 1996.
hero_note: Read the 2021–22 spike carefully. Norwegian income per head at PPP went from $69,890 in 2020 to $128,470 in 2022 and then fell back to $107,770 — a swing of roughly 70 points against the EU average and back again in four years. It sits exactly on the European energy price spike, and Norway is a large net exporter of oil and gas. Nothing about the country's productive capacity changed by 84% in two years.

name: Iceland
status: Applied in 2009 after the banking collapse, suspended talks in 2013, and holds an advisory referendum on resuming them on 29 August 2026.
notes: In the single market through the EEA since 1994. Fisheries stay outside, which is the central unresolved question.
hero_note: The 2008 collapse is the largest single movement on this page: 128% of the EU average in 2007, 104% by 2010. Iceland's EU application followed it by nine months, and the application was suspended once the economy had recovered — which is why this country's position on membership is hard to read off its income line.

name: Switzerland
status: Rejected the EEA by referendum in 1992 and built a bilateral route instead — more than a hundred separate agreements, renegotiated one at a time.
notes: Free movement of persons since 2002, Schengen since 2008, no customs union, no EEA. A new package of agreements was signed on 2 March 2026 and is not yet ratified.
hero_note: Switzerland starts higher than any EU member and falls through the period — from 179% of the EU average in 2000 to 156% in 2025. That is mostly the denominator: the EU average itself rose as poorer members caught up. Against the fixed US benchmark on the Overview tab, Switzerland gained 6.5 points rather than losing 23.
